tools.name: ScheduleWakeup
tools.description:
Schedule when to resume work in /loop dynamic mode — the user invoked /loop without an interval, asking you to self-pace iterations of a specific task.

Do NOT schedule a short-interval wakeup to poll for background work you started — when harness-tracked work finishes, you are re-invoked automatically, so polling is wasted. Instead schedule a long fallback (1200s+) so the loop survives if the work hangs or never notifies. The exception is external work the harness cannot track (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue) — there, pick a delay matched to how fast that state actually changes.

Pass the same /loop prompt back via `prompt` each turn so the next firing repeats the task. For an autonomous /loop (no user prompt), pass the literal sentinel `<<autonomous-loop-dynamic>>` as `prompt` instead — the runtime resolves it back to the autonomous-loop instructions at fire time. (There is a similar `<<autonomous-loop>>` sentinel for CronCreate-based autonomous loops; do not confuse the two — ScheduleWakeup always uses the `-dynamic` variant.) To end the loop, call this tool with `stop: true` (omit every other field) — the loop ends immediately and no further wakeups fire.

Set `noop: true` if nothing changed — you checked and there's nothing to report ("no change", "still waiting", "quiet hold"). Set `noop: false` if something happened worth keeping — you edited a file, posted a message, advanced state, or surfaced a finding. Consecutive `noop: true` ticks are collapsed in the user's terminal view and tracked as a streak, so long quiet holds stay legible to the user without scrolling. Omit `noop` when stopping (`stop: true`).

## Picking delaySeconds

This session's requests use a 1-hour Anthropic prompt-cache TTL, so effectively every allowed delay (the runtime clamps to [60, 3600]) wakes up with your conversation context still cached. There is no cache cliff inside that range to pace around, and scheduling extra wakeups just to keep the cache warm is pure waste — never do that. (If the session enters usage overage, later requests drop to the 5-minute TTL; don't try to track or preempt that — the guidance here stays the same.)

Match the delay to what you're actually waiting for:

- **Actively polling external state the harness can't notify you about** (a CI run, a deploy, a remote queue): pick the delay from how fast that state actually changes. A CI run that takes ~8 minutes deserves one ~480s check, not eight 60s ones.
- **The long fallback heartbeat** (something else — a Monitor, a task notification — is the primary wake signal): 1200s+, so quiet wakeups stay rare.
- **Idle ticks with no specific signal to watch**: default to **1200s–1800s** (20–30 min). The loop still checks back regularly, and the user can always interrupt if they need you sooner.

Don't think in cache windows — think about what you're actually waiting for.

## The reason field

One short sentence on what you chose and why. Goes to telemetry and is shown back to the user. "watching CI run" beats "waiting." The user reads this to understand what you're doing without having to predict your cadence in advance — make it specific.

tools.description:
Invoke a skill.

A skill is a packaged set of instructions the user or project has set up for a particular kind of task (deploy steps, a review checklist, a repo-specific workflow). Available skills appear in a listing from the system with one-line descriptions. When the task at hand is one a listed skill covers, call this tool first — the skill's instructions load into the turn for you to follow in place of your default approach; some skills instead run in a subagent and return the finished result. A skill that runs in the background returns only the agent's name — its result arrives later as a task notification, so don't wait on it or invoke it again in the meantime. Users may also ask for one by name (`/<name>`, or "slash command"); that's a request to invoke it.

- `args`: optional arguments to pass through.

Only names from the listing (or that the user typed explicitly) are valid. Built-in CLI commands (`/help`, `/clear`, …) aren't skills. If a `<command-name>` block is already present this turn, the skill is loaded — follow it directly rather than calling again.

I'm weighing whether to raise the video upload limit: GitHub only embeds mp4s through its web uploader, so a raw link won't render inline, and a GIF would embed but loses quality. Next I'm thinking about the perf section, since "every PR, no matter what" doesn't fit docs-only or test-only changes, which can't touch runtime. I'd want a noise threshold too, or small measurement swings would keep triggering endless loops, and the perf-interactions check costs real AI calls, so it should only run when chat is touched.

content.text:
I think this is a good change. Three things in it need deciding before I write it. The repo already has most of the tooling: `scripts/perf-pages.mjs` measures page loads (median TTFB, FCP, LCP, time to heading, JS bytes, desktop and mobile), and `scripts/perf-interactions.mjs` measures the Ask panel, chat, mic and polling.

## Proposed changes

**1. `AGENTS.md`: a new "Speed" section, under Tests.**

> ## Speed
>
> Every PR reports speed before and after, measured on production builds of `main` and the branch against the seeded QA backend, never on `next dev`:
>
> - **Opening the app:** `node scripts/perf-pages.mjs 5 before=<main> after=<branch>`. It measures the pages listed in the script in one interleaved run, so machine noise hits both builds the same way.
> - **What the change touches:** time the action itself, like opening the panel, importing a file, a chat answer or a sync, with `perf-interactions.mjs` or a small Playwright timing.
>
> Report the medians in a before/after table. A slowdown counts when a median is more than 10% **and** more than 50 ms worse, or the JS bytes grow. If you find one, fix it before opening the PR. Speed is part of done, not a follow-up. If it can't be fixed, explain why in the PR and ask the owner.

**2. `AGENTS.md`, in "Commits and pull requests":**

> - UI changes put their screenshots (light and dark, desktop and mobile) and a short video or GIF of the flow in the PR description itself, embedded so they show inline. A path to a local file doesn't count. Capture them from the QA workspace only: the repo is public, so never show the owner's data.

I'd also change the "Goal-driven" line ("Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot") to point to this rule.

**3. A new `.github/pull_request_template.md`** with empty **Speed** (before/after table) and **Visuals** sections, so every PR starts with the slots to fill.

## What needs your call

1. **Do docs-only PRs need speed numbers?** You said "no matter what". I'd still keep the Speed section in every PR, but let docs- or test-only PRs write "no runtime change". Running two production builds for a README edit costs about 10 minutes and tells you nothing.
2. **How should images get into the PR?** GitHub only allows uploading attachments through the web page, not through `gh` or the API. Agents would have to push the files to a separate `pr-assets` branch and embed the raw links. PNGs and GIFs show inline that way; an MP4 shows only as a link. My suggestion: use GIFs for flows, and MP4 links only for long recordings.
3. **Interaction timings can cost money.** Measuring chat or voice makes real AI calls, which goes against the "mock in tests" rule. I'd allow them only when the PR changes chat or voice, with at most 3 runs.

Tell me your answers, or "go with your suggestions", and I'll make the edits on a branch and open the PR.

# AGENTS.md

Moneo is an open-source personal-finance app you run on your own computer. One owner imports statements or syncs a bank, tracks accounts and wealth, plans spending, and asks about their money in chat, artifacts and voice calls.

Moneo ships two ways from this one codebase: the desktop app (`desktop/`, Electron, what most owners install) and the source installation (`npm run setup` + Docker). Every change must work in both.

Stack: Next.js 16 + React 19 + TypeScript. The backend is Postgres plus the open-source Supabase Auth, PostgREST and Storage services: in Docker for the source installation (`docker-compose.yml`), as bundled native processes in the desktop app (`desktop/src/backend/`). Drizzle schema, Workflow (local world) for durable jobs, Vitest and Playwright, and the Vercel AI SDK, paid by the owner's ChatGPT plan or an API key.

These are defaults. The developer's instructions override them; if a rule conflicts with the task, say so and ask.

## Non-negotiables

- **Local-first.** Everything listens on `127.0.0.1`; optional phone access is Tailscale forwarding to it (`lib/phone-access.ts`). Data leaves the machine only for services the owner set up (AI provider, Enable Banking, Scalable). New features must work fully offline from the cloud except those calls.
- **One owner, no accounts.** The proxy signs the owner in automatically; there is no sign-up or sign-in screen. Private access from the owner's own Tailscale devices needs no login; anything public must add one first.
- **Financial truth comes from code and data, never from AI guesses.** Money is integer minor units (`bigint`) with an explicit currency. The AI explains and proposes; every write it suggests is a card the owner accepts.
- **AI organization labels are the one exception to cards.** The organizer applies high- and medium-confidence category and merchant labels itself, marked as AI (`organized_by = 'ai'`), listed with every other AI decision and undoable; they never become owner rules or owner corrections. Every other AI write is a card.
- **History is kept.** Preserve source records, corrections, history and undo when changing financial data flows.
- **Open source.** No secrets, private statements or personal data in the repo (`npm run check:privacy` runs before tests and lint).

## How to work

1. **Think before coding.** State your assumptions. If a request has more than one reading, name them and ask instead of picking silently. If a simpler approach exists, say so.
2. **Simplicity first.** Write the least code that solves the problem: no speculative features, options or single-use abstractions. Prefer existing utilities and dependencies, and Zod for validating user and external input. Would a senior engineer call it overcomplicated? Then simplify.
3. **Surgical changes.** Touch only what the task needs and match the nearby style. Remove what your own change made unused; mention unrelated dead code instead of deleting it.
4. **Never write a comment.** Put the meaning in a name, a type, a test or a lint rule; if a comment would defend a workaround, fix the cause instead. `npm run lint` rejects comments (`moneo/no-comments` in `eslint.config.mjs`) except tool directives such as `eslint-disable-next-line <rule> -- reason`.
5. **Corrections become checks.** When a review correction could recur, enforce it with a lint rule, a type or a test whose error message says what to do instead. Add a line here only when it needs human judgment.
6. **Fix the class, not the case.** Trace a failure to the first place the system went wrong and fix it there, so every similar case is fixed with it. A guard, a retry, a swallowed error or a special case at the place it showed up hides the fault. When the assistant in the app cannot do something, give it the tool, data or scope it lacks; never add a sentence to its system prompt (`lib/ai/provider.ts`, `lib/ai/voice-*`) that names one request, keyword or example.
7. **Goal-driven.** Turn the task into checks you can run, then loop until they pass. A bug fix starts by reproducing the failure; see Tests for when that becomes a kept test. Purely visual changes get a before/after screenshot instead.

## Safety

- Never run tests or experiments against the owner's backend (`.env`, Docker project `moneo`, app on port 3000). Tests use the separate test backend below, as its QA user or disposable users they create and remove.
- Never delete the `moneo` Docker volumes (`docker compose down -v`) or drop its database: that is the owner's financial history. The test backend is disposable: `docker compose -p moneo-qa down -v` then `npm run setup -- --qa` starts it fresh.
- Never change `JWT_SECRET`, `POSTGRES_PASSWORD` or `BANK_TOKEN_ENCRYPTION_KEY` in an existing `.env`; keys, sessions and stored bank and ChatGPT tokens stop working.
- Never commit `.env*` (except `.env.example`), `.data/`, `e2e/.auth.json` or `.qa/`.
- Only kill processes you started, or ones you verified by port and working directory. Never kill by name.
- Real AI, bank and Scalable calls cost money or count against limits (PSD2 allows about 4 background bank fetches a day). Mock them in tests unless the task is to check the real service.

## Hit every surface

Before calling a feature done, check where else it shows up:

- Pages and their mobile layout, light and dark.
- Chat tools and the system prompt in `lib/ai/provider.ts`, artifacts, and the voice call (`lib/ai/voice-*`).
- Home widgets and the command palette.
- Background jobs (`lib/scheduler.ts`, `workflows/`) and imports from files, banks and Scalable.
- The desktop app: see Desktop app below.
- The reverse path: undo, reset all data, reconnect, disconnect.
- Docs: `README.md` for anything the owner sets up or runs, the landing page in `docs/` when a headline feature or install step changes, `.env.example` for new variables. Deferred work goes in GitHub issues.

## Commands

Use npm (`package-lock.json` is authoritative).

- Install: `npm ci`
- Backend: `npm run setup` (writes `.env` secrets, starts Docker, applies migrations, creates the owner; safe to rerun)
- Dev: `npm run dev` (http://localhost:3000)
- Unit: `npm test` · Lint: `npm run lint` · Build: `npm run build` · Bundle budget: `npm run check:bundle` (after a build)
- Database: `npm run test:db` (needs the backend from `npm run setup`)
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)
- Desktop: `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform <win-x64|mac-arm64|mac-x64|linux-x64>` once, then `npm run desktop:build`, `npm run desktop:dev`, `npm run desktop:dist` and `npm run desktop:smoke` (drives the packaged app)
- Desktop release: push a `v*` tag matching `desktop/package.json`, then publish the drafted release (`desktop/README.md` → Releasing). Never tag or publish unasked.

## Test backend

Everything that needs a database or a running app is tested against `moneo-qa`, never the owner's setup:

- **Backend:** Docker project `moneo-qa` (ports 54521/54522), secrets in the git-ignored `.env.qa` (one shared copy in `~/.moneo/qa.env`, so every worktree uses the same stack). Create, upgrade or copy it into a new worktree with `npm run setup -- --qa`; then `npm run qa:auth` creates the QA user and saves `e2e/.auth.json`.
- **App:** `npm run qa:server` runs this checkout on http://localhost:3100 against `.env.qa`, building into `.next-qa`, with bank access off and a placeholder AI key that every provider rejects, so nothing costs money. `npm run test:e2e` starts it on its own and refuses to run against any server that would sign tests in as the owner.
- **Screenshots:** `npm run qa:shots -- <label> home money/transactions` saves each page in light, dark and mobile to `.qa/shots/<label>/` and fails on a console error or a failed request (skill `verify-ui`).
- **Reset:** `npm run qa:reset` empties the QA workspace. Each spec should still set up the state it needs rather than rely on what earlier runs left behind.
- `npm run test:db` and the `supabase/tests/*.mjs` scripts read `.env.qa` only.
- A nightly run (`npm run qa:nightly`, see `e2e/README.md`) runs every spec twice and keeps the issue "Nightly browser suite is failing" up to date; fix what it lists before adding new specs.

## Desktop app

The Electron app (`desktop/README.md`, `desktop/src/backend/README.md`) runs the same Next.js server as a standalone build next to its own Postgres, GoTrue, PostgREST and Storage processes. There is no Docker, Node.js, terminal or `.env` on the owner's machine, so:

- **Settings the owner needs go in the app**, not in `.env`. `desktop:build` unsets every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` and fails if a local address is baked in; desktop-only behaviour reads `MONEO_DESKTOP_*` at runtime.
- **Migrations run on the owner's existing database** at the next start, after an automatic `pre-upgrade` backup (`desktop/src/backend/migrations.ts`). They must work without the extensions the bundle lacks: supautils, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, pgsodium/vault, pg_stat_statements, realtime, and uuid-ossp on Windows.
- **The app lives on `http://localhost:47300`** (or the port saved in `shell.json`), not 3000. Get addresses from the request or from `appUrl()`, `loopbackUrl()` and `appPort()` in `lib/env.ts`; lint rejects a hard-coded 3000.
- **Sign-ins open in the system browser** and return through the loopback callbacks; the result reaches the window through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`. The window opens only Moneo's own pages and allows only the microphone and copying.
- **Files the server reads at runtime** by a dynamic path need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`, or the standalone build traces source files and `desktop:build` fails.
- **A new backend service, native module or data folder** must be added to `fetch-backend.mjs`, the start order, backup and restore, and the packaged files in `electron-builder.config.cjs`.
- **Keep the security fuses** (RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` off; asar integrity on); `desktop:smoke` reads them back.
- Never test against the owner's installed app or its user-data folder; set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.

The Desktop workflow builds and smoke-tests every platform on pull requests that touch `desktop/`, `scripts/desktop/`, `next.config.ts`, `package*.json` or `supabase/migrations/`.

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `components/` — shared UI
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions
- `desktop/` — the Electron app (`src/` main process, `src/backend/` native backend, `setup/` status window, `bootstrap/` first-run SQL); `scripts/desktop/` builds, packages and smoke-tests it; `.github/workflows/desktop.yml` runs that and drafts releases
- `docs/` — the GitHub Pages landing page (https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/); its download button reads the latest published release

Imports go one way: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`. `lib/finance/` never imports `lib/ai/`, and Electron stays in `desktop/src`. Lint enforces all of it (`moneo/import-boundaries`); code that two layers need lives in the lower one.

## Rules and what enforces them

When a correction could recur, enforce it (skill `review-to-rule`) and add a row here. A rule with nothing in the right-hand column is only a hope.

| Rule | Enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| No comments, except exact tool directives | `moneo/no-comments` (lint, autofix) |
| `app/` → `components/` → `lib/`, `workflows/`; `lib/finance` never imports `lib/ai`; Electron only in `desktop/`; no app code in `desktop/src` | `moneo/import-boundaries` (lint) |
| The modules every page loads (`lib/auth`, `lib/settings`, `lib/safe-action`, `lib/env`) never import `lib/ai` | `moneo/import-boundaries` (lint) |
| Dates use the owner's time zone from Settings (detected from their device, saved on first load); no function assumes one | required `timeZone` parameters (compiler); `no-restricted-syntax` (lint) |
| No hard-coded port 3000 or app address outside `lib/env.ts` | `no-restricted-syntax` (lint) |
| Tests never wait on a real timer, skip from inside a test, read migration text, or touch port 3000 | `no-restricted-syntax` (lint) |
| One way to make a database client: `serviceDb()` for the service role, `createClient()` in `lib/supabase-server.ts` for the owner | `no-restricted-imports` (lint) |
| Every scheduled route checks the cron secret, through `cronRoute()` | `lib/cron.test.ts` walks every route; `no-restricted-properties` (lint) |
| A workflow never ignores a failure without naming what handles it | `no-restricted-syntax` (lint, `workflows/`) |
| No `eslint-disable` that suppresses nothing | `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` (lint) |
| Every code path returns; overrides are marked; no switch fall-through | `tsconfig.json` |
| A stored preference this version cannot read never blocks sign-in | `lib/settings.test.ts` |
| The assistant's system prompt does not grow by special cases | budget in `lib/ai/provider.test.ts` |
| `lib/schema.ts` matches the migrated database; app and database agree on currency minor units; SQL conflicts are never raised as `40001` | `lib/schema.live.test.ts` (`npm run test:db`, CI job `database`) |
| No secrets, statements or personal data in the repo | `npm run check:privacy` (runs before test and lint) |
| A page's JavaScript stays within its size budget | `npm run check:bundle` |
| A test file runs in 10 seconds or less | CI, "Slowest test files" |

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Desktop app**: the same callbacks on the app's own port (47300 by default) instead of 3000.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Tests

A test earns its place by failing when real behaviour breaks. Before writing one, name the bug it would catch.

- **Write tests for** money math, imports and undo, auth, RLS and AI scopes, concurrency, and bugs that actually happened (name the PR or issue).
- **Don't write tests that** assert UI copy or labels, grep source or migration files, mirror the implementation, or need more than about three `vi.mock`s to run. Test the `lib/` function instead.
- Check each test against two imagined edits. Break the behaviour (a wrong value, a skipped or doubled effect): the test must fail. Restructure the internals without changing any result: the test must still pass. Rewrite or delete a test that misses either. Take the expected value from the requirement, never from a run of the code, and never assert on data the test built itself.
- One test per behaviour. Don't add a test per requirement or per audit finding; if an existing test covers the failure, extend it.
- `npm test` must pass with no `.env`, no Docker and no network. Anything that needs the database is a `*.live.test.ts`.
- Use fake timers or controlled promises, never real waits. Mock AI, bank and Scalable; real calls are opt-in only.
- Browser specs are for whole user journeys, not single links or labels. Add a spec only when no existing journey can take the check.
- When you remove a feature, remove its tests. Never delete or skip a failing test just to get green: fix the cause, or ask.
- If a pointless test lands, find out why the agent wrote it and fix the guidance here.

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. CI runs the same checks on every pull request, and `npm run test:db` against a fresh test backend.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Deferred work gets their issue created on github.
- Stacked PRs: before merging a PR that another open PR is based on, change the dependent PR's base to `main`; deleting the merged branch otherwise closes it.
- Long agent prompts and plans don't get committed; if guidance must persist, put the rule in AGENTS.md.
- suggest edits in agents.md if there was something that is changed or needs to be there in agents.md but only suggest when it is actually needed dont suggest just for suggesting.(only for prs)

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

- Database: `npm run test:db` (needs the backend from `npm run setup`)
- E2E: `npm run test:e2e` (see `e2e/README.md`)
- Desktop: `node scripts/desktop/fetch-backend.mjs --platform <win-x64|mac-arm64|mac-x64|linux-x64>` once, then `npm run desktop:build`, `npm run desktop:dev`, `npm run desktop:dist` and `npm run desktop:smoke` (drives the packaged app)
- Desktop release: push a `v*` tag matching `desktop/package.json`, then publish the drafted release (`desktop/README.md` → Releasing). Never tag or publish unasked.

## Test backend

Everything that needs a database or a running app is tested against `moneo-qa`, never the owner's setup:

- **Backend:** Docker project `moneo-qa` (ports 54521/54522), secrets in the git-ignored `.env.qa` (one shared copy in `~/.moneo/qa.env`, so every worktree uses the same stack). Create, upgrade or copy it into a new worktree with `npm run setup -- --qa`; then `npm run qa:auth` creates the QA user and saves `e2e/.auth.json`.
- **App:** `npm run qa:server` runs this checkout on http://localhost:3100 against `.env.qa`, building into `.next-qa`, with bank access off and a placeholder AI key that every provider rejects, so nothing costs money. `npm run test:e2e` starts it on its own and refuses to run against any server that would sign tests in as the owner.
- **Screenshots:** `npm run qa:shots -- <label> home money/transactions` saves each page in light, dark and mobile to `.qa/shots/<label>/` and fails on a console error or a failed request (skill `verify-ui`).
- **Reset:** `npm run qa:reset` empties the QA workspace. Each spec should still set up the state it needs rather than rely on what earlier runs left behind.
- `npm run test:db` and the `supabase/tests/*.mjs` scripts read `.env.qa` only.
- A nightly run (`npm run qa:nightly`, see `e2e/README.md`) runs every spec twice and keeps the issue "Nightly browser suite is failing" up to date; fix what it lists before adding new specs.

## Desktop app

The Electron app (`desktop/README.md`, `desktop/src/backend/README.md`) runs the same Next.js server as a standalone build next to its own Postgres, GoTrue, PostgREST and Storage processes. There is no Docker, Node.js, terminal or `.env` on the owner's machine, so:

- **Settings the owner needs go in the app**, not in `.env`. `desktop:build` unsets every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` and fails if a local address is baked in; desktop-only behaviour reads `MONEO_DESKTOP_*` at runtime.
- **Migrations run on the owner's existing database** at the next start, after an automatic `pre-upgrade` backup (`desktop/src/backend/migrations.ts`). They must work without the extensions the bundle lacks: supautils, pg_graphql, pg_net, pg_cron, pgsodium/vault, pg_stat_statements, realtime, and uuid-ossp on Windows.
- **The app lives on `http://localhost:47300`** (or the port saved in `shell.json`), not 3000. Get addresses from the request or from `appUrl()`, `loopbackUrl()` and `appPort()` in `lib/env.ts`; lint rejects a hard-coded 3000.
- **Sign-ins open in the system browser** and return through the loopback callbacks; the result reaches the window through `lib/desktop-bridge.ts` and `desktop/src/bridge.ts`. The window opens only Moneo's own pages and allows only the microphone and copying.
- **Files the server reads at runtime** by a dynamic path need `/*turbopackIgnore: true*/`, or the standalone build traces source files and `desktop:build` fails.
- **A new backend service, native module or data folder** must be added to `fetch-backend.mjs`, the start order, backup and restore, and the packaged files in `electron-builder.config.cjs`.
- **Keep the security fuses** (RunAsNode, `NODE_OPTIONS` and `--inspect` off; asar integrity on); `desktop:smoke` reads them back.
- Never test against the owner's installed app or its user-data folder; set `MONEO_DESKTOP_HOME` to a scratch folder.

The Desktop workflow builds and smoke-tests every platform on pull requests that touch `desktop/`, `scripts/desktop/`, `next.config.ts`, `package*.json` or `supabase/migrations/`.

## Project map

- `app/` — App Router pages, route handlers, server actions
- `components/` — shared UI
- `lib/finance/` — deterministic financial logic
- `lib/ai/` — models, chat tools, ChatGPT sign-in (`chatgpt.ts`), voice
- `lib/bank/`, `lib/scalable/` — Enable Banking and Scalable Capital
- `lib/schema.ts` + `supabase/migrations/` — database schema
- `workflows/` — durable background jobs; `lib/scheduler.ts` runs the daily ones
- `docker-compose.yml`, `docker/`, `scripts/setup.mjs` — the self-hosted backend
- `e2e/` — Playwright flows; `supabase/tests/` — SQL regressions
- `desktop/` — the Electron app (`src/` main process, `src/backend/` native backend, `setup/` status window, `bootstrap/` first-run SQL); `scripts/desktop/` builds, packages and smoke-tests it; `.github/workflows/desktop.yml` runs that and drafts releases
- `docs/` — the GitHub Pages landing page (https://indkhan.github.io/Moneo/); its download button reads the latest published release

Imports go one way: `app/` → `components/` → `lib/` and `workflows/`. `lib/finance/` never imports `lib/ai/`, and Electron stays in `desktop/src`. Lint enforces all of it (`moneo/import-boundaries`); code that two layers need lives in the lower one.

## Rules and what enforces them

When a correction could recur, enforce it (skill `review-to-rule`) and add a row here. A rule with nothing in the right-hand column is only a hope.

| Rule | Enforced by |
| --- | --- |
| No comments, except exact tool directives | `moneo/no-comments` (lint, autofix) |
| `app/` → `components/` → `lib/`, `workflows/`; `lib/finance` never imports `lib/ai`; Electron only in `desktop/`; no app code in `desktop/src` | `moneo/import-boundaries` (lint) |
| The modules every page loads (`lib/auth`, `lib/settings`, `lib/safe-action`, `lib/env`) never import `lib/ai` | `moneo/import-boundaries` (lint) |
| Dates use the owner's time zone from Settings (detected from their device, saved on first load); no function assumes one | required `timeZone` parameters (compiler); `no-restricted-syntax` (lint) |
| No hard-coded port 3000 or app address outside `lib/env.ts` | `no-restricted-syntax` (lint) |
| Tests never wait on a real timer, skip from inside a test, read migration text, or touch port 3000 | `no-restricted-syntax` (lint) |
| One way to make a database client: `serviceDb()` for the service role, `createClient()` in `lib/supabase-server.ts` for the owner | `no-restricted-imports` (lint) |
| Every scheduled route checks the cron secret, through `cronRoute()` | `lib/cron.test.ts` walks every route; `no-restricted-properties` (lint) |
| A workflow never ignores a failure without naming what handles it | `no-restricted-syntax` (lint, `workflows/`) |
| No `eslint-disable` that suppresses nothing | `reportUnusedDisableDirectives` (lint) |
| Every code path returns; overrides are marked; no switch fall-through | `tsconfig.json` |
| A stored preference this version cannot read never blocks sign-in | `lib/settings.test.ts` |
| The assistant's system prompt does not grow by special cases | budget in `lib/ai/provider.test.ts` |
| `lib/schema.ts` matches the migrated database; app and database agree on currency minor units; SQL conflicts are never raised as `40001` | `lib/schema.live.test.ts` (`npm run test:db`, CI job `database`) |
| No secrets, statements or personal data in the repo | `npm run check:privacy` (runs before test and lint) |
| A page's JavaScript stays within its size budget | `npm run check:bundle` |
| A test file runs in 10 seconds or less | CI, "Slowest test files" |

## Sign-in callbacks and addresses

Each outside service sends the browser back to a different address. Keep these in mind before changing ports, hosts or remote access:

- **Sign in with ChatGPT** (`lib/ai/chatgpt.ts`): OpenAI only accepts the loopback `http://127.0.0.1:<PORT>/api/ai/chatgpt/callback`, so sign-in happens on the computer running Moneo. Tokens are stored there, so chat works from any device afterwards.
- **Enable Banking** (`lib/bank/return-listener.ts`): production apps need an `https://` redirect registered in the Enable Banking app. Moneo uses `https://localhost:3443/api/bank/callback` (a local listener with a cert from `npm run setup`), which forwards to `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL`.
- **Scalable Capital** (`lib/scalable/server.ts`): dynamic client registration with `NEXT_PUBLIC_APP_URL/api/scalable/callback`. `localhost` registers freely; other hosts need Scalable's allowlist (it rejects `*.ts.net`).
- **Supabase** (`NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `127.0.0.1:54321`): only the server may call it; never send the browser there, or it breaks on other devices.
- **Desktop app**: the same callbacks on the app's own port (47300 by default) instead of 3000.
- **Phone and tablet** (`*.ts.net` through Tailscale Serve): the laptop's addresses above never change. The three logins refuse to start from a remote device (`lib/remote-device.ts`) and say to use the computer; everything else, including sync, works from there.
- **Voice** needs a secure context (https or localhost) for the microphone.

## Database changes

Add a new ordered migration in `supabase/migrations/` and keep `lib/schema.ts` aligned. Never rewrite an applied migration. `npm run setup` applies pending ones and records them in `supabase_migrations.schema_migrations`. For other Supabase CLI commands use `npx supabase ... --db-url "$SUPABASE_DB_URL"` (from `.env`).

## Tests

A test earns its place by failing when real behaviour breaks. Before writing one, name the bug it would catch.

- **Write tests for** money math, imports and undo, auth, RLS and AI scopes, concurrency, and bugs that actually happened (name the PR or issue).
- **Don't write tests that** assert UI copy or labels, grep source or migration files, mirror the implementation, or need more than about three `vi.mock`s to run. Test the `lib/` function instead.
- Check each test against two imagined edits. Break the behaviour (a wrong value, a skipped or doubled effect): the test must fail. Restructure the internals without changing any result: the test must still pass. Rewrite or delete a test that misses either. Take the expected value from the requirement, never from a run of the code, and never assert on data the test built itself.
- One test per behaviour. Don't add a test per requirement or per audit finding; if an existing test covers the failure, extend it.
- `npm test` must pass with no `.env`, no Docker and no network. Anything that needs the database is a `*.live.test.ts`.
- Use fake timers or controlled promises, never real waits. Mock AI, bank and Scalable; real calls are opt-in only.
- Browser specs are for whole user journeys, not single links or labels. Add a spec only when no existing journey can take the check.
- When you remove a feature, remove its tests. Never delete or skip a failing test just to get green: fix the cause, or ask.
- If a pointless test lands, find out why the agent wrote it and fix the guidance here.

Run the smallest relevant test while iterating. Before finishing, run `npm test`, `npm run lint` and `npm run typecheck`; add `npm run build` for app, config or build changes, and Playwright for changed user flows. CI runs the same checks on every pull request, and `npm run test:db` against a fresh test backend.

## Commits and pull requests

- Break the work into steps and commit each one; a big task is several commits.
- Write commit messages in plain language: what changed and why.
- Deferred work gets their issue created on github.
- Stacked PRs: before merging a PR that another open PR is based on, change the dependent PR's base to `main`; deleting the merged branch otherwise closes it.
- Long agent prompts and plans don't get committed; if guidance must persist, put the rule in AGENTS.md.
- suggest edits in agents.md if there was something that is changed or needs to be there in agents.md but only suggest when it is actually needed dont suggest just for suggesting.(only for prs)

## Context

Read only what the task needs: `.env.example` for environment names, `e2e/README.md` for browser tests, `supabase/tests/README.md` for SQL checks.

=== verify-ui
---
name: verify-ui
description: Prove a Moneo change works by driving the real QA app the way the owner would, and attach the evidence (screenshots in light, dark and mobile, or a recording) to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a change in the running app

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. "It compiles" and "the tests pass" are not proof; pictures and recordings of the real app are.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## 1. Launch

`npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. It is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:3100/api/health` prints 401 or 200.

If port 3100 is already taken, another checkout's QA app owns it and serves that checkout's code. Do not kill it. Start this checkout's app on a free port and point the tools at it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`.

## 2. Doctor

Run this whenever anything looks off, before changing code:

`npm run qa:shots -- doctor home`

It fails with the reason when the app is not worth driving:

- **"The QA session was not accepted"**: the saved session expired (they last an hour). Run `npm run qa:auth`.
- **Every page is the "could not sign you in" screen after a fresh `qa:auth`**: the shared QA workspace holds data this checkout cannot read. Run `npm run qa:reset`.
- **A failed request or console error on an untouched page**: the base is broken. Fix or report that first; evidence taken on a broken base proves nothing.

## 3. Drive

1. **List the pages.** Every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names.
2. **Set up the state.** If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does. An empty page proves an empty page.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base):
   `npm run qa:shots -- before home money/transactions`
   Name pages without the leading slash (Git Bash rewrites `/paths`); `home` is `/`.
4. **After.** On the changed code, the same command with `after`.

Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`, prints the HTTP status and every failed request or console error per page, and exits 1 if there were any.

**A flow, not a page.** A screenshot cannot show a tap, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and record it:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## 4. Evidence

- Use the path the owner uses: real pages, real buttons. Not a test-only endpoint or a direct database write for the step under test.
- Capture the action and the state it leaves, not only the last screen.
- Check the side effects next to what is visible: the row written, the history entry, what undo restores.
- **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
- When something looks wrong, suspect the capture before the app, and measure the live page before reporting a bug.

## 5. Hand over

Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, with one line on what to look at. Attach the video for a flow. Upload by dragging the files into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them. Say which pages you covered, what changed in each and what you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the server you started, found by its port and this checkout's path, never by name. Leave `.qa/shots/` in place: cleanup removes instances, never the evidence.

Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.

Read `.agents/skills/verify-ui/SKILL.md` in this repository and follow it. (It lives there so Codex and other agents use the same steps.)
=== review-to-rule
---
name: review-to-rule
description: Turn a correction into something the codebase enforces (a better design, a type, a lint rule or a test) so it never needs saying again. Use when the owner corrects a mistake, says "stop doing X", "always do Y" or "make this a rule", when the same fix is needed a second time, or when the tempting fix is another sentence in AGENTS.md or in the assistant's system prompt.
---

# Turn a correction into a check

Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example and takes the shortest path that compiles. A sentence in AGENTS.md is read sometimes; a check runs every time. The instruction is the symptom: change the code so the mistake cannot be made.

This applies to the product as well. When the assistant in the app gets a request wrong, a sentence in its system prompt (`lib/ai/provider.ts`, `lib/ai/voice-*`) naming that request is the same symptom fix. See step 2.

## Steps

1. **Name the class, not the case.** State the rule in one sentence with its reason. Then find every other place with the same fault: grep for the pattern, and check recent commits, reverts and review comments for earlier instances. If you cannot say why it matters, ask the owner before building anything.
2. **Fix it at the highest level that works**, in this order:
   - **Design.** Give each piece of state one owner and each job one supported way. Replace hand-synced lists with one source of truth. Delete the old way and any dead code an agent would copy. For the in-app assistant: give it the tool, the data or the scope it lacked, so this request and every similar one works.
   - **A type.** Make the wrong code fail to compile: a required parameter instead of a default, a narrowed or branded type, a function that only accepts the safe input.
   - **A lint rule** in `eslint.config.mjs`, when wrong code still compiles. `moneo/import-boundaries` covers "this may not import that"; `no-restricted-syntax` with an AST selector covers "this call or shape is not allowed"; `no-restricted-properties` covers one member. Add a rule to the `moneo` plugin only when a selector cannot express it.
   - **A test**, when the rule is about behaviour. Follow AGENTS.md Tests.
   - **Prose in AGENTS.md**, last, only for judgment calls. Nothing fails when an agent skips it.

   In your reply, say which level you picked and why the one above it did not work.
3. **Write the error for an agent.** It says what is wrong, why, and the file, type or function to use instead, and it names the AGENTS.md section. "Don't do X" alone gets an `eslint-disable`.
4. **Fix every existing violation in the same change.** A rule with a pile of disables teaches that disabling is normal. If there are too many, scope the rule to the folders that are already clean, or make it fail only when a change adds more, and open an issue for the rest.
5. **Prove the check fails on the real mistake.** Reproduce the original mistake (the old line, the old import) and watch the check reject it; then confirm the fixed code passes.
   `printf '%s\n' 'import { a } from "@/app/page"; export const b = a;' | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename lib/sample.ts`
   Two config blocks that match one file replace each other's options for the same rule, so try a file from every folder the rule should cover.
6. **Update the rule table** in AGENTS.md ("Rules and what enforces them"): add the rule with its check. If the rule was there as a sentence, replace the sentence with the table row. Remove a row once the mistake can no longer be written at all.
7. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.

## Do not

- Add an `eslint-disable`, a guard, a retry or a swallowed error to get to green.
- Add a sentence to a system prompt that names one request, keyword or example to make that one case work.
- Write a check that greps source text or asserts copy.
- Encode a one-off preference about this diff. If it will not recur, just fix the code.

=== state-chart
---
name: state-chart
description: Draw the state machine of a Moneo flow as a diagram the owner can review, taken from the code, and list the paths that break a rule. Use when a change adds or alters a multi-step flow (import, bank connect and reconnect, Scalable orders, proposal cards, voice call, agent runs, desktop start-up), when asked to "draw the states", "show the flow" or "state chart", or to show a bug as a path through states.
---

# Draw a flow's state machine

The owner decides whether the behaviour is right, so the chart is in their words. Build it from the code, never from memory of how the flow should work.

## Steps

1. **Write the rules first.** List what must always hold, in sentences the owner would agree with: "an order is sent at most once", "undo puts back exactly what the import added", "nothing is written until the card is accepted". These are what the chart is checked against.
2. **Find where the state lives.** Usually a status column in `lib/schema.ts` (and its check constraint in `supabase/migrations/`), a union type, or a workflow in `workflows/`. List every value it can take.
3. **Find every transition.** Grep for each write to that status and each place it is compared. For each one record: from, to, what triggers it and the file and line.
4. **Walk it for holes.** Answer each from the code:
   - Is every state reachable, and can every state that is not final be left?
   - What happens on failure, on a second tap, and when two devices act at once?
   - What do undo, disconnect and "reset all data" do from each state?
   - What happens if the app quits mid-transition and starts again?

---
name: verify-ui
description: Prove a Moneo change works by driving the real QA app the way the owner would, and attach the evidence (screenshots in light, dark and mobile, or a recording) to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a change in the running app

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. "It compiles" and "the tests pass" are not proof; pictures and recordings of the real app are.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## 1. Launch

`npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. It is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:3100/api/health` prints 401 or 200.

If port 3100 is already taken, another checkout's QA app owns it and serves that checkout's code. Do not kill it. Start this checkout's app on a free port and point the tools at it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`.

## 2. Doctor

Run this whenever anything looks off, before changing code:

`npm run qa:shots -- doctor home`

It fails with the reason when the app is not worth driving:

- **"The QA session was not accepted"**: the saved session expired (they last an hour). Run `npm run qa:auth`.
- **Every page is the "could not sign you in" screen after a fresh `qa:auth`**: the shared QA workspace holds data this checkout cannot read. Run `npm run qa:reset`.
- **A failed request or console error on an untouched page**: the base is broken. Fix or report that first; evidence taken on a broken base proves nothing.

## 3. Drive

1. **List the pages.** Every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names.
2. **Set up the state.** If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does. An empty page proves an empty page.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base):
   `npm run qa:shots -- before home money/transactions`
   Name pages without the leading slash (Git Bash rewrites `/paths`); `home` is `/`.
4. **After.** On the changed code, the same command with `after`.

Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`, prints the HTTP status and every failed request or console error per page, and exits 1 if there were any.

**A flow, not a page.** A screenshot cannot show a tap, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and record it:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## 4. Evidence

- Use the path the owner uses: real pages, real buttons. Not a test-only endpoint or a direct database write for the step under test.
- Capture the action and the state it leaves, not only the last screen.
- Check the side effects next to what is visible: the row written, the history entry, what undo restores.
- **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
- When something looks wrong, suspect the capture before the app, and measure the live page before reporting a bug.

## 5. Hand over

Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, with one line on what to look at. Attach the video for a flow. Upload by dragging the files into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them. Say which pages you covered, what changed in each and what you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the server you started, found by its port and this checkout's path, never by name. Leave `.qa/shots/` in place: cleanup removes instances, never the evidence.

---
name: review-to-rule
description: Turn a correction into something the codebase enforces (a better design, a type, a lint rule or a test) so it never needs saying again. Use when the owner corrects a mistake, says "stop doing X", "always do Y" or "make this a rule", when the same fix is needed a second time, or when the tempting fix is another sentence in AGENTS.md or in the assistant's system prompt.

# Turn a correction into a check

Assume the next contributor is an agent that sees only the files it opened, copies the nearest example and takes the shortest path that compiles. A sentence in AGENTS.md is read sometimes; a check runs every time. The instruction is the symptom: change the code so the mistake cannot be made.

This applies to the product as well. When the assistant in the app gets a request wrong, a sentence in its system prompt (`lib/ai/provider.ts`, `lib/ai/voice-*`) naming that request is the same symptom fix. See step 2.

## Steps

1. **Name the class, not the case.** State the rule in one sentence with its reason. If you cannot say why it matters, ask the owner before building anything.
2. **Fix it at the highest level that works**, in this order:
   - **Design.** Give each piece of state one owner and each job one supported way. Replace hand-synced lists with one source of truth. Delete the old way and any dead code an agent would copy. For the in-app assistant: give it the tool, the data or the scope it lacked, so this request and every similar one works.
   - **A type.** Make the wrong code fail to compile: a required parameter instead of a default, a narrowed or branded type, a function that only accepts the safe input.
   - **A lint rule** in `eslint.config.mjs`, when wrong code still compiles. `moneo/import-boundaries` covers "this may not import that"; `no-restricted-syntax` with an AST selector covers "this call or shape is not allowed"; `no-restricted-properties` covers one member. Add a rule to the `moneo` plugin only when a selector cannot express it.
   - **A test**, when the rule is about behaviour. Follow AGENTS.md Tests.
   - **Prose in AGENTS.md**, last, only for judgment calls. Nothing fails when an agent skips it.

   In your reply, say which level you picked and why the one above it did not work.
3. **Write the error for an agent.** It says what is wrong, why, and the file, type or function to use instead, and it names the AGENTS.md section. "Don't do X" alone gets an `eslint-disable`.
4. **Fix every existing violation in the same change.** A rule with a pile of disables teaches that disabling is normal. If there are too many, scope the rule to the folders that are already clean, or make it fail only when a change adds more, and open an issue for the rest.
5. **Prove the check fails on the real mistake.** Reproduce the original mistake (the old line, the old import) and watch the check reject it; then confirm the fixed code passes.
   `printf '%s\n' 'import { a } from "@/app/page"; export const b = a;' | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename lib/sample.ts`
   Two config blocks that match one file replace each other's options for the same rule, so try a file from every folder the rule should cover.
6. **Update the rule table** in AGENTS.md ("Rules and what enforces them"): add the rule with its check. If the rule was there as a sentence, replace the sentence with the table row. Remove a row once the mistake can no longer be written at all.
7. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.

## Do not

- Add an `eslint-disable`, a guard, a retry or a swallowed error to get to green.
- Add a sentence to a system prompt that names one request, keyword or example to make that one case work.
- Write a check that greps source text or asserts copy.
- Encode a one-off preference about this diff. If it will not recur, just fix the code.

Takes before/after screenshots in light, dark and mobile with `npm run qa:shots`, records Playwright video for flows, and the agent must look at every picture. | The "Screenshots" line in Test backend names it. It adds a row to that table for each new rule. |
| **state-chart** | Draws a flow's state machine from the code as a Mermaid diagram, finds paths that break a rule, and puts the chart in the PR before and after. | Nothing in AGENTS.md mentions it; agents find it only from its own description. |

**The gap you noticed is in verify-ui step 5.** It says to drag the files into the PR or "ask the owner to", because `.qa/` is never committed. That's why PRs end up saying "the images are in this folder".

+   - **A lint rule** in `eslint.config.mjs`, when wrong code still compiles. `moneo/import-boundaries` covers "this may not import that"; `no-restricted-syntax` with an AST selector covers "this call or shape is not allowed"; `no-restricted-properties` covers one member. Add a rule to the `moneo` plugin only when a selector cannot express it.
+   - **A test**, when the rule is about behaviour. Follow AGENTS.md Tests.
+   - **Prose in AGENTS.md**, last, only for judgment calls. Nothing fails when an agent skips it.
+   In your reply, say which level you picked and why the one above it did not work.
+3. **Write the error for an agent.** It says what is wrong, why, and the file, type or function to use instead, and it names the AGENTS.md section. "Don't do X" alone gets an `eslint-disable`.

+4. **Fix every existing violation in the same change.** A rule with a pile of disables teaches that disabling is normal. If there are too many, scope the rule to the folders that are already clean, or make it fail only when a change adds more, and open an issue for the rest.
+5. **Prove the check fails on the real mistake.** Reproduce the original mistake (the old line, the old import) and watch the check reject it; then confirm the fixed code passes.
+   `printf '%s\n' 'import { a } from "@/app/page"; export const b = a;' | npx eslint --stdin --stdin-filename lib/sample.ts`
+   Two config blocks that match one file replace each other's options for the same rule, so try a file from every folder the rule should cover.

+6. **Update the rule table** in AGENTS.md ("Rules and what enforces them"): add the rule with its check. If the rule was there as a sentence, replace the sentence with the table row. Remove a row once the mistake can no longer be written at all.
+7. Run `npm run lint`, `npm run typecheck` and `npm test`.
+## Do not
+- Add an `eslint-disable`, a guard, a retry or a swallowed error to get to green.
+- Add a sentence to a system prompt that names one request, keyword or example to make that one case work.
+- Write a check that greps source text or asserts copy.
+- Encode a one-off preference about this diff. If it will not recur, just fix the code.
+name: state-chart

+description: Draw the state machine of a Moneo flow as a diagram the owner can review, taken from the code, and list the paths that break a rule. Use when a change adds or alters a multi-step flow (import, bank connect and reconnect, Scalable orders, proposal cards, voice call, agent runs, desktop start-up), when asked to "draw the states", "show the flow" or "state chart", or to show a bug as a path through states.
+# Draw a flow's state machine
+The owner decides whether the behaviour is right, so the chart is in their words. Build it from the code, never from memory of how the flow should work.
+## Steps

+1. **Write the rules first.** List what must always hold, in sentences the owner would agree with: "an order is sent at most once", "undo puts back exactly what the import added", "nothing is written until the card is accepted". These are what the chart is checked against.

+2. **Find where the state lives.** Usually a status column in `lib/schema.ts` (and its check constraint in `supabase/migrations/`), a union type, or a workflow in `workflows/`. List every value it can take.
+3. **Find every transition.** Grep for each write to that status and each place it is compared. For each one record: from, to, what triggers it and the file and line.
+4. **Walk it for holes.** Answer each from the code:
+   - Is every state reachable, and can every state that is not final be left?
+   - What happens on failure, on a second tap, and when two devices act at once?
+   - What do undo, disconnect and "reset all data" do from each state?
+   - What happens if the app quits mid-transition and starts again?
+   For each rule from step 1, look for the shortest path of steps that breaks it. A question the code does not answer is a finding. Never weaken a rule or tidy the chart to hide one.
+5. **Draw it** as Mermaid `stateDiagram-v2`.
+   - Label a state with what the owner sees or cares about ("Reviewing", "Order sent, answer unknown"), not a variable name. Add the stored value in brackets only when it helps.
+   - Label an arrow with the step as the owner sees it happen: "you confirm", "the bank says no", "Moneo restarts". Not a function name.
+   - Mark the arrows the AI triggers and the ones that need an accepted card.
+   - Aim for 20 arrows or fewer. Merge states that behave the same; never merge two states that break different rules.
+   - Give every state that breaks a rule the class `breaks`.
+   ```mermaid
+   stateDiagram-v2
+     classDef breaks fill:#fde2e2,stroke:#b42318
+     [*] --> Uploaded
+     Uploaded --> Reviewing: columns recognised
+     Uploaded --> Failed: file unreadable
+     Reviewing --> Imported: you confirm
+     Imported --> Uploaded: you undo
+     Reviewing --> Stuck: Moneo restarts
+     class Stuck breaks
+6. **Replay each broken path against the real code.** Write it as a failing test or a live repro, one step per arrow. If the bug does not happen, assume the chart is wrong until you show it is not.

+7. **Hand it over.** In the PR description or in chat (rendered, not as source, when a preview tool is available): the chart, one line per broken rule with its path, and what the chart leaves out. When a change alters a flow, show the chart before and after.
+## Do not
+- Commit the chart to the repo. It goes stale like a comment; draw it again from the code.
+- Invent states or transitions to make the picture tidy.
+name: verify-ui

+description: Prove a Moneo change works by driving the real QA app the way the owner would, and attach the evidence (screenshots in light, dark and mobile, or a recording) to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
+# Verify a change in the running app
+The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. "It compiles" and "the tests pass" are not proof; pictures and recordings of the real app are.
+Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.
+## 1. Launch

+`npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. It is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:3100/api/health` prints 401 or 200.

+If port 3100 is already taken, another checkout's QA app owns it and serves that checkout's code. Do not kill it. Start this checkout's app on a free port and point the tools at it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`.
+## 2. Doctor
+Run this whenever anything looks off, before changing code:
+`npm run qa:shots -- doctor home`
+It fails with the reason when the app is not worth driving:
+- **"The QA session was not accepted"**: the saved session expired (they last an hour). Run `npm run qa:auth`.
+- **Every page is the "could not sign you in" screen after a fresh `qa:auth`**: the shared QA workspace holds data this checkout cannot read. Run `npm run qa:reset`.
+- **A failed request or console error on an untouched page**: the base is broken. Fix or report that first; evidence taken on a broken base proves nothing.
+## 3. Drive
+1. **List the pages.** Every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names.
+2. **Set up the state.** If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does. An empty page proves an empty page.
+3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base):
+   `npm run qa:shots -- before home money/transactions`
+   Name pages without the leading slash (Git Bash rewrites `/paths`); `home` is `/`.
+4. **After.** On the changed code, the same command with `after`.

+Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`, prints the HTTP status and every failed request or console error per page, and exits 1 if there were any.
+**A flow, not a page.** A screenshot cannot show a tap, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and record it:
+`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`
+Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).
+## 4. Evidence
+- Use the path the owner uses: real pages, real buttons. Not a test-only endpoint or a direct database write for the step under test.
+- Capture the action and the state it leaves, not only the last screen.
+- Check the side effects next to what is visible: the row written, the history entry, what undo restores.

+- **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
+- When something looks wrong, suspect the capture before the app, and measure the live page before reporting a bug.
+## 5. Hand over

+Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, with one line on what to look at. Attach the video for a flow. Upload by dragging the files into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them. Say which pages you covered, what changed in each and what you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.
+## 6. Clean up
+Stop only the server you started, found by its port and this checkout's path, never by name. Leave `.qa/shots/` in place: cleanup removes instances, never the evidence.

content.text:
`instrumentation.ts` is the file Next.js runs once when the server starts. On `main` it sets up five things:

1. **Database connections stay open for a minute** instead of 4 seconds, so each page doesn't pay for new connections.
2. **A reverse-DNS lookup is turned off**, because it could freeze the server while Workflow looks for its local port.
3. **Desktop preview builds stop here**, so a private desktop preview doesn't sync banks or start other background work.
4. **Background jobs start:** Workflow resumes unfinished runs, then the daily scheduler starts (summaries and bank/Scalable syncs).
5. **The `https://localhost:3443` listener starts**, which real banks send you back to.

`instrumentation.test.ts` checks the same points: the DNS setting, the startup order, that a startup failure is reported, and the desktop-preview skip.

**Your uncommitted change** moved that code into a new `instrumentation.node.ts`, so the Edge build never reads it. It was written against the old `main`, and since then `main` has moved on:

- it lacks the desktop-preview skip, so private desktop previews would start bank syncs again;
- it still has comments, which lint now rejects;
- the test still imports `register` from `instrumentation.ts` and expects the old behaviour.

I saved it in a git stash (`stash@{0}`) instead of discarding it, then fast-forwarded `main` to `ef266dc4`. Nothing is lost: `git stash pop` brings it back.

**My suggestion:** drop that stash. `main`'s version already does everything the split did. The split is only worth redoing if an Edge build error made you write it; if so, tell me and I'll redo it on top of the current code.

The check of AGENTS.md and the skills you asked for is still to come; I'll do that next unless you want to settle this first.

content.text:
`main` is now at `ef266dc4` and the stash is gone. I went through AGENTS.md, the three new skills, CI and the recent PRs.

## What I found

- **Images:** the verify-ui skill takes good screenshots, but then says to drag them into the PR on GitHub "or ask the owner to". Agents can't drag, so the images never get into the PR. PR #250 is an example: it says "Files are in `.qa/shots/228/`" and shows no images.
- **Speed:** nothing in AGENTS.md or the skills asks for speed numbers. The scripts exist (`perf-pages.mjs`, `perf-interactions.mjs`), but nothing points to them. `perf-interactions.mjs` also makes real AI calls, and the QA app has no mock AI to time against.
- **Nothing checks either rule.** AGENTS.md itself says a rule nothing enforces is "only a hope".

## What I'd do

1. **Images go into the PR itself.** Change step 5 of verify-ui: push the pictures to a `pr-assets` branch and embed their links in the PR description, so they show inline. Screenshots go in as PNGs. A flow goes in as a video link plus one still frame, because inline GIFs need ffmpeg, which this machine doesn't have.
2. **New `measure-speed` skill.** It runs a production build of `main` and one of the branch on QA data, and puts a before/after table in the PR:
   - how long the app takes to open (`perf-pages.mjs`);
   - how long the touched action takes, with AI, bank and Scalable mocked.

   A slowdown means more than 10% **and** more than 50 ms worse, or more JavaScript. The agent must fix a slowdown before opening the PR, or explain why it can't and ask you. Docs-only PRs skip this.
3. **AGENTS.md:** one line each pointing to measure-speed and verify-ui, under "Commits and pull requests".
4. **A CI check on the PR description.** It fails a code PR with no Speed table, and a UI PR with no images. That is what makes the rule stick.
5. **Mock AI for the QA app.** A small code change so interaction timings never cost money. It's code, not docs, so it gets its own PR.

My order: 1–3 in one docs PR, then 5, then 4.

What I'd like to settle with you:

- Is 10% and 50 ms the right threshold for a slowdown?
- Do you want the CI check (4), or are the skills enough?
- Is a separate `pr-assets` branch in this public repo fine with you? It holds QA data only, but it will keep growing.

---
name: measure-speed
description: Measure how fast Moneo opens and how fast the changed action runs, before and after a change, and put the numbers in the pull request. Use before opening any PR that changes code, when asked "is it faster", "measure speed" or "check performance", and when a change could slow a page, an import, a sync, a chat answer or start-up.
---

# Measure speed before and after

Every change should leave Moneo as fast as before or faster. Measure it; never guess. A PR that only changes docs (`*.md`, `docs/`) skips this and writes "No runtime change" under Speed.

Everything runs against the QA backend, never port 3000, on production builds: `next dev` compiles each page on its first visit and makes everything look slow.

## 1. Two builds

- **After:** this checkout. `QA_PORT=3101 npm run qa:server -- --production` in the background.
- **Before:** the PR's base in its own worktree: `git worktree add ../moneo-speed-base origin/main`, then in it `npm ci`, `npm run setup -- --qa` (copies `.env.qa`) and `QA_PORT=3102 npm run qa:server -- --production` in the background.

Both use the same QA workspace, so they see the same data. Each is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:<port>/api/health` prints 401 or 200. Run `npm run qa:auth` if the session is older than an hour.

Set up the data the change needs the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does, through the app. An empty page measures an empty page.

## 2. Opening the app

`node scripts/perf-pages.mjs 5 before=http://localhost:3102 after=http://localhost:3101`

It loads every main page cold on desktop and mobile, the two builds interleaved run by run so machine noise hits both alike, and prints the medians: TTFB, first paint, LCP, time until the heading shows, layout shift, long tasks and JS KB. The full results are in `.qa/perf-before.json` and `.qa/perf-after.json`.

## 3. What the change touches

Time the action the change affects, from the owner's tap until its result shows: opening a panel, an import, accepting a card, a sync, a chat answer. Use Playwright against both ports, one warm-up and then at least 5 runs each, and take the median.

Mock AI, bank and Scalable with `page.route`, the way `e2e/*.mocked.spec.ts` does, so nothing costs money and the number is Moneo's own time, not the provider's. `scripts/perf-interactions.mjs` makes real AI calls: run it only when the owner asks.

For work with no screen (a workflow step, a `lib/` function), time it with a small script against the QA backend, both checkouts, same runs and median.

## 4. Read the numbers

A slowdown is a median more than 10% **and** more than 50 ms worse, or more JS on a page. Anything smaller is noise; when in doubt, run again.

A slowdown means this change made Moneo slower. Find the cause (a trace with `--trace on`, the Network tab, the React Profiler) and fix it before opening the PR, then measure again. If the extra time cannot be avoided, say in the PR what costs it and why, and ask the owner.

## 5. Hand over

Add this to the PR description:

```markdown
## Speed

Production builds on QA data, median of 5 runs. Before: `<base sha>`. After: `<head sha>`.

| What | Before | After | Change |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Open Home, desktop (heading shows) | 640 ms | 610 ms | −5% |
| Open Home, mobile | 820 ms | 800 ms | −2% |
| Accept a cash card (tap → new balance) | 310 ms | 290 ms | −6% |
```

List Home, every page the change touches and the action from step 3. Put any slowdown first, with its cause.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the servers you started, found by port and checkout path, never by name. Remove the base worktree with `git worktree remove ../moneo-speed-base`.

name: verify-ui
description: Prove a Moneo change works by driving the real QA app the way the owner would, and attach the evidence (screenshots in light, dark and mobile, or a recording) to the pull request. Use after any change to a page, component, style or user flow, when asked to "verify", "show me it works" or "add screenshots", and before opening a PR that changes what the owner sees.
---

# Verify a change in the running app

The owner reviews what the app does, not the diff. "It compiles" and "the tests pass" are not proof; pictures and recordings of the real app are.

Everything here runs against the QA app on http://localhost:3100. Never use port 3000; that is the owner's app and data.

## 1. Launch

`npm run setup -- --qa`, then `npm run qa:auth`, then `npm run qa:server` in the background. It is ready when `curl -s -o /dev/null -w "%{http_code}" -H "x-moneo-test: 1" http://localhost:3100/api/health` prints 401 or 200.

If port 3100 is already taken, another checkout's QA app owns it and serves that checkout's code. Do not kill it. Start this checkout's app on a free port and point the tools at it with `E2E_BASE_URL=http://localhost:<port>`.

## 2. Doctor

Run this whenever anything looks off, before changing code:

`npm run qa:shots -- doctor home`

It fails with the reason when the app is not worth driving:

- **"The QA session was not accepted"**: the saved session expired (they last an hour). Run `npm run qa:auth`.
- **Every page is the "could not sign you in" screen after a fresh `qa:auth`**: the shared QA workspace holds data this checkout cannot read. Run `npm run qa:reset`.
- **A failed request or console error on an untouched page**: the base is broken. Fix or report that first; evidence taken on a broken base proves nothing.

## 3. Drive

1. **List the pages.** Every route the change can affect, including the ones AGENTS.md "Hit every surface" names.
2. **Set up the state.** If a page needs data, create it the way the nearest spec in `e2e/` does. An empty page proves an empty page.
3. **Before.** With the change set aside (a temporary commit on another branch, or `git worktree add` of the base):
   `npm run qa:shots -- before home money/transactions`
   Name pages without the leading slash (Git Bash rewrites `/paths`); `home` is `/`.
4. **After.** On the changed code, the same command with `after`.

Each run writes `<page>-light.png`, `<page>-dark.png` and `<page>-mobile.png` to `.qa/shots/<label>/`, prints the HTTP status and every failed request or console error per page, and exits 1 if there were any.

**A flow, not a page.** A screenshot cannot show a tap, a card being accepted or an undo. Extend the journey spec in `e2e/` that already covers the flow and record it:

`npx playwright test e2e/<spec> --workers=1 --trace on --video on`

Add a new spec only when no existing journey can take the check (AGENTS.md Tests).

## 4. Evidence

- Use the path the owner uses: real pages, real buttons. Not a test-only endpoint or a direct database write for the step under test.
- Capture the action and the state it leaves, not only the last screen.
- Check the side effects next to what is visible: the row written, the history entry, what undo restores.
- **Look at every picture yourself.** Read each PNG. Check for overflow, clipped text, unreadable contrast in dark and a broken layout on mobile. A console error or a status of 400 or more is a failure: fix it and shoot again.
- When something looks wrong, suspect the capture before the app, and measure the live page before reporting a bug.

## 5. Hand over

Put before and after side by side in the PR description for each page that visibly changed, with one line on what to look at. Attach the video for a flow. Upload by dragging the files into the PR on GitHub, or ask the owner to if you cannot; `.qa/` is git-ignored, so never commit them. Say which pages you covered, what changed in each and what you could not capture and why. If nothing visibly changed, say so and attach nothing.

## 6. Clean up

Stop only the server you started, found by its port and this checkout's path, never by name. Leave `.qa/shots/` in place: cleanup removes instances, never the evidence.
